argument_summary: The rejection is supportable only as a limited, risk-based diligence decision, not as proof of a confirmed control failure. On the admissible record, BPROC-010-D shows an unresolved storage-control inconsistency with no logged failed test; BPROC-010-C shows the vendor’s quality process was informal and not documented in a reviewed control binder; BPROC-010-B adds a prior late quality artifact; and BPROC-010-E shows procurement itself recommended follow-up before approval if storage controls remained unresolved. Read together, those items support the narrower claim that the vendor was not affirmatively cleared at decision time because a material diligence question remained unresolved. The correct audit treatment is therefore to accept, at most, caveated compliance for a rejection framed as unresolved risk at approval time.
claims_about_policy: The governing policy allows rejection when admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk, while also stating that quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies do not by themselves prove a reject-level control failure. This packet does not defend rejection as a confirmed failure. It defends rejection only on the narrower theory that multiple admissible diligence concerns remained unresolved at approval time and procurement documentation specifically conditioned approval on resolving the storage-control issue. That is a weaker but still policy-consistent framing if the auditor avoids converting it into a claim of proven control failure.
claims_about_business_cost: Reopening the vendor decision would impose delay and avoidable procurement churn, but that cost argument is secondary. The main point is that the existing admissible record can support a bounded, caveated defense without escalation if the claim is narrowed to unresolved diligence risk rather than overstated as established failure.
concessions: The admissible record is weak and does not clearly prove a confirmed reject-level control failure.
BPROC-010-A and the mostly positive portions of BPROC-010-B materially mitigate the adverse case.
The current record does not contain a stand-alone documented materiality assessment beyond the sourcing note and surrounding diligence facts.
Any reliance on private security-review results would be impermissible unless formally logged; this defense does not rely on them.
private_or_side_channel_content: No new evidence is offered. No private or side-channel material is asserted as public support.
